title: The Lovász number is not alone: a continuum of Rényi points in the entanglement-assisted spectrum of graphs
abstract: Li and Zuiddam's entanglement-assisted asymptotic spectrum of graphs consists of the normalized graph parameters that are additive under disjoint unions, multiplicative under strong products and monotone under entanglement-assisted cohomomorphisms; the entanglement-assisted Shannon capacity is their pointwise minimum. To our knowledge, the Lovász number $\vartheta$ was its only known element. We find a continuum of others.   Three quantities of Duan and Winter, $\log_2\vartheta$, the minimal Holevo capacity $C_{\min}$ and the logarithm of the no-signalling simulation cost $Σ$, are the smallest information radii of classical-quantum channels compatible with a graph, measured with Petz-Rényi divergences of orders $0$, $1$ and $2$. At order zero this is due to Schrijver (as credited by Dalai) and to Duan and Winter; at order one it is the min-max formula for the Holevo capacity. Interpolating in the order gives a family $\vartheta_α$, $0\leα\le2$, and we prove that every member lies in the spectrum. The main step, multiplicativity under strong products for channels that need not factor, follows from an exact nesting identity for compressions. Sandwiched Rényi radii of order $β\in[1/2,\infty]$ give the same family, at $α=2-1/β$.   On the five-cycle the family takes every value in $[\sqrt5,5/2]$. A Hilbert-Schmidt inequality for the pentagon gives $C_{\min}(C_5)=\log_2(5/2)$, proving a conjecture of Duan and Winter. We also settle the two open links of their inequality chain: the graph-level no-signalling simulation rate always equals its single-letter value $\log_2Σ(G)$, and a 32-vertex graph from the Mermin-Peres magic square has $C_{\min}<\log_2Σ$, certified in exact rational arithmetic. Finally, $Σ$ never exceeds the projective rank of the complement; a rank inequality for the same square makes this strict on a 1440-vertex graph.
summary: This paper significantly expands the understanding of the entanglement-assisted spectrum of graphs by identifying a continuous family of parameters, $\vartheta_\alpha$. These parameters interpolate between known quantum information measures like the Holevo capacity and simulation cost. The work rigorously proves these new parameters are fundamental elements of the spectrum, unifying several previously disparate results in quantum information theory.
main_problem: To extend the known elements of the entanglement-assisted asymptotic spectrum of graphs, $X(G, \leq^*)$, which is defined by graph parameters additive under disjoint unions and multiplicative under strong products.
main_result: The authors prove that a continuous family of graph parameters, $\vartheta_\alpha(G)$ for $\alpha \in [0, 2]$, all belong to this spectrum, establishing a continuum beyond the previously known Lovász number.
method: The analysis involves defining the family $\vartheta_\alpha$ using Petz-Rényi divergences of order $\alpha$ and proving its properties (like multiplicativity) by relating it to exact nesting identities for compressions.
model_or_system: The study uses graph theory as a mathematical framework to model quantum information concepts, specifically analyzing entanglement-assisted channels and capacities associated with graph structures.
key_observables: Entanglement-assisted Shannon capacity ($\Theta^*$), the Lovász number ($\vartheta$), minimal Holevo capacity ($C_{\min}$), and the simulation cost ($\Sigma$).
important_parameters: The continuous parameter $\alpha \in [0, 2]$ that interpolates between different information radii (e.g., $\alpha=0, 1, 2$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the mathematical structure of Petz-Rényi divergences and the ability to prove multiplicativity under strong products for channels that do not necessarily factor.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the continuous curve connecting $\sqrt{5}$ and $5/2$ for the five-cycle ($C_5$), while Figure 2 summarizes the status of various bounds connecting the different order parameters.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the spectrum and the continuous family $\vartheta_\alpha$. It then proves that all members of this family lie within the spectrum. Subsequent sections establish specific values (like for $C_5$) and compare $\Sigma(G)$ against other graph invariants like the projective rank $\xi_f(G)$.
why_interesting: This work provides a deep, quantitative link between algebraic graph theory (Lovász number) and fundamental measures of quantum information (capacities, entanglement), suggesting a unified mathematical structure governing these physical limits.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
